title: Meta Releases Muse Glimmer: A Local, Agentic, Multimodal, and Open Source AI Model
summary: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, a 30B-parameter multimodal AI model designed for local, agentic use cases. Distilled from the larger Muse model and released under the Apache 2.0 license, it supports text, image, and video inputs, along with multimodal tool calling and object detection. The model is optimized for privacy-aware applications like coding, document analysis, and personal assistants. It features a hybrid attention architecture, speculative decoding for faster inference, and broad compatibility with libraries like Transformers, llama.cpp, vLLM, and Inference Endpoints. Benchmarks show competitive performance in agentic, coding, multimodal, and safety tasks.
key_points: Muse Glimmer is a 30B-parameter multimodal model by Meta, released under Apache 2.0 for local deployment.
Designed for agentic use cases: coding, document analysis, personal assistants, and privacy-aware applications.
Supports text, image, and video inputs, with capabilities like multimodal tool calling and object detection.
Architecture includes a 2B ViT-style vision encoder and a 28B text decoder with hybrid attention (sliding window + full attention).
Features speculative decoding (DFlash) for faster generation, especially useful for structured content like coding.
Day-0 support in Transformers, llama.cpp, vLLM, and Inference Endpoints for easy integration.
Benchmarks demonstrate strong performance in agentic, coding, multimodal reasoning, and safety tasks.
Optimized for local deployment with reduced costs and privacy benefits; supports NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel GPUs.
Includes practical guides for text-only, image, video, and tool-calling inference, as well as fine-tuning with TRL.
Supports tensor-parallel serving and managed deployments via Hugging Face Inference Endpoints.
